messages.author: bf7c0a7b58a65524
messages.subject: Failure of Local NBLAST installation
parts:
Dear NBLAST community/ Dr Jefferis,

I am having issues getting NBLAST to work on any platform. 

The online version returns, "An error has occurred. Check your logs or contact the app author for clarification". 

Accordingly, I tried to set up NBLAST to work off my desktop instead. However, whenever I try to upload a tracing, select my template and press "NBLAST", I get the message: "Error in cmtk.streamxform: Error running CMTK streamxform!".I had previously failed to get the CMTK plugin for fiji to work on windows so thought that this may be the issue. 

>cmtk.bindir() returns: [1] "C:\\Program Files\\CMTK-3.3\\CMTK\\lib\\cmtk\\bin"
> cmtk.dof2mat(version = TRUE) returns: [1] "3.3.1"

Finally, I attempted to set up NBLAST on my linux desktop, as here I was able to get the CMTK fiji plugin to work. However, I receive. "Error in find_bridgin_path: sample template: T1 has no bridgin registrations"- this likley results from an inability to download the template brains, which results in the following error: Error in git2r::clone(url, localdir, ...) : Error in 'git2r_clone': there is no TLS stream available. 

I have hit a bit of a wall in my ability to progress and would really appreciate any help, preferably in getting the windows version to work but failing this the linux or online version. It is worth noting that my setup of the  desktop version of NBLAST functions for pairwise comparison/ one against all - the issues arise for "upload a tracing".

Best Wishes,
George.

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: Failure of Local NBLAST installation
parts:
Dear George,

Thanks for your interest in nat / NBLAST. Sorry to hear of all these installation / online NBLAST issues and the slow response. It sounds like you have been a bit unlucky with install issues on Windows. Although R and the natverse packages are cross platform, the developers and most users are on macosx or linux and some external dependencies including CMTK and in this case apparently git can be fiddly on Windows. We can try to walk you through the install issues, but if you want to sidestep them and get started quickly, can I suggest that you try out a new option:

https://hub.docker.com/r/natverse/r-natverse

This is a self-contained Docker image. It should allow you to install R + RStudio and the complete natverse suite with all external dependencies in 3 steps and a few minutes of download time. Once again I have not been able to test the docker image on Windows yet, but so long as your Windows systems is new enough to install Docker, it should work out of the box (and I would be happy for feedback).

In terms of the online NBLAST, I can confirm that searching by uploading a tracing has stopped working this week. The VFB developer recently overhauled the NBLAST on the fly virtual machine and it seems something broke in the process. I do not have access to that machine so it is hard to debug, but I have asked him to check.

Briefly in terms of your local install issues

1. It looks like you have CMTK installed as Windows application but our recommendation for use with the natverse is to install via cygwin. See http://natverse.org/nat/articles/Installation.html#cmtknat-on-windows
2. For git2r/libgit I see a few people with similar looking error messages e.g. https://github.com/ropensci/git2r/issues/410. The implication is that there was something off with your installation of libgit2 and openssl. Do you know if you installed the git2r package as a binary or from source?

With best wishes,

Greg.
